With the explicit score from \({\rm def:pc-handle}\),
\[
 \widehat\theta_h
 =\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}

defs.def:pc-handle:
Conditionally on \(A\), put \(X=Z-\tfrac12\mathbf1_n\), \(P_A=\widehat\Pi_r(A)\), and \(C_A=P_AA\).  For every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), define
\[
 \widetilde\gamma_{i,h}=q_{i,h}-4(C_AX)_i.

Fix \(0\leq m\leq\lfloor d/2\rfloor\) and write
\[

\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\theta-\theta_n|
 \geq \frac{c a_m}{n}\mathbb E_P\sqrt{K_m(A)}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac1n\mathbb E_P\sqrt{K_m(A)}
 \leq\sqrt{\frac{n^{-1}\mathbb E_PK_m(A)}{n}}
 \leq\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{m,n}}{n}}.
\]

defs.def:empirical-projector:
Order the eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix \(A\) by decreasing absolute value, breaking equal-absolute-value ties by decreasing signed value.  Within every remaining repeated eigenspace, choose the orthonormal basis obtained by applying Gram--Schmidt to the nonzero vectors in the ordered list of projections of \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) onto that eigenspace.  Let \(\widehat\Psi_r(A)\) contain the first \(r\) resulting orthonormal eigenvectors and define
\[
 \widehat\Pi_r(A)=\widehat\Psi_r(A)\widehat\Psi_r(A)^\top.
\]
This deterministic tie rule makes \(A\mapsto\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) a fixed Borel-measurable sample map.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(I_0(A)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}\).  Under the repaired class, any graph-only radius \(b(A)\) that is required to satisfy
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z(\widetilde\theta-\theta_n\mid A,(f_i)_i)\right|\leq b(A)
\]
for every response configuration in the conditional support must obey
\[
 b(A)\geq \frac{B}{n}I_0(A)
\]
on every realized graph.  Whenever \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) is nonempty, the independent-Rademacher response submodel \(f_i(a,x)=\varepsilon_iBx\) is admissible, and even a genie revealing every nonisolate sign leaves, conditionally on \(A\), Bayes absolute-error risk between
\[
 \frac{B}{\sqrt3\,n}\sqrt{I_0(A)}
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad
 \frac{B}{n}\sqrt{I_0(A)}.
\]
Thus the corresponding unconditional missing-sign fluctuation is of order \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E\sqrt{I_0(A)}\), which is no larger than the expected conditional radius \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E I_0(A)\).  This distinction neither constructs an unconditionally honest interval nor proves that every such interval must pay the graph-only conditional radius.

\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
At each index the proof fixes the graph primitives of an arbitrary admissible member, retains its kernel \(W\) and the independent \({\rm Uniform}[0,1]\) latent types, and changes only the response law.  For almost every \(u\),
\[
 N_i\mid U_i=u
 \sim{\rm Binomial}\!\left(n-1,\rho_n\int_0^1W(u,v)\,dv\right),
 \qquad
 \frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{\kappa}
 \leq\mathbb E(N_i\mid U_i=u)
 \leq(n-1)\rho_n\kappa.
\]
These uniform conditional-degree bounds, together with explicit linear, local \(C^3\)-bump, and degree-lattice response pairs, give respectively the graph, interior, and lattice terms for both minimax absolute risk and minimax honest expected length. \[

 \qquad

\]
Suppose, in addition to the conditions defining \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), that
\[
 c_0\leq\kappa,
 \qquad
 b_\psi\geq (r-1)/\sqrt r.
\]
Let \(s_0=B/4\), let \(\xi_i\) be i.i.d. with density \(p_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1}\cos^2(\pi t/(2s_0))\mathbf 1\{|t|\leq s_0\}\), and use response pairs \(f_i^\pm(a,x)=\xi_i\pm g(x)\), with the three functions \(g\) constructed in the proof.  Then \(W_0\) and these random-intercept response laws generate an explicit block submodel of \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\).  Along sequences with \(B,L,r,\kappa,\underline\lambda,b_\psi,\alpha,C_{\log}\) fixed and \(C_{\log}\log n\leq d=o(n)\), there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(n\) and \(d\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
Within this same block submodel, respectively, a degree-lattice bump, an interior \(C^3\) bump, and a linear response pair furnish the lattice term, the interior nonlinear term for both absolute risk and honest expected length, and the graph floor. For \(L>0\), at every sufficiently large triangular-array index the supported-unit component satisfies \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp Ld^{-2}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\leq d^{-1}\), \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), and \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\geq d^{-1/2}\).  At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\), the explicit degree-exact procedure proves
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \leq2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\]
Along every sequence covered by the unrestricted supported converse, there is a constant \(c>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
Every graph-only conditional-bias certificate over the repaired class retains at least \(Bn^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}\) on a realized graph. The exact moment equation \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]=0\) also cancels every quadratic exposure response, with affine responses as a special case.  At \(h_\star=d^{-1/2}\), the analytic nonremainder score and graph terms both have order \(\sqrt{d/n}\), while the complete corrected certificate is
\[
 \overline b_{h_\star}(A)=\frac Bn\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}+\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h_\star},
 \qquad
 \overline s_{h_\star}(A)^2=\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h_\star}
 =\frac1{4n^2}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V_n}
 \left(\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\beta_{ij,h_\star}\right)^2.
\]
No sharp stochastic order is asserted for the last display.  An affine realized law inside \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) with \(L>0\) does not permit setting the honesty radius to zero; the reduction applies only when \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\) is fixed before observing the experiment.

Conditionally on \(A\), write \(X_j=Z_j-1/2\), \(X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)^\top\), and \(q_h=(q_{1,h},\ldots,q_{n,h})^\top\).  For a centered scalar function \(g(X)\), define its first projection as \(g^{(1)}=\sum_j\mathbb E[g\mid X_j]\) and its second projection as
\[
 g^{(2)}=\sum_{j<k}\left\{\mathbb E[g\mid X_j,X_k]
 -\mathbb E[g\mid X_j]-\mathbb E[g\mid X_k]\right\},
\]
and apply these definitions coordinatewise to a vector.  The first two conditional Hoeffding projections of the exact-support score satisfy
\[
 q_h^{(1)}=4AX,\qquad q_h^{(2)}=0
\]
simultaneously for every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\).  Consequently, for every \(A\)-measurable orthogonal projector \(\Pi\),
\[
 \{(I_n-\Pi)q_h\}^{(1)}=4(I_n-\Pi)AX,
 \qquad \{(I_n-\Pi)q_h\}^{(2)}=0,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_Z\!\left[\|4(I_n-\Pi)AX\|_2^2\mid A\right]
 =4\|(I_n-\Pi)A\|_{\mathrm F}^2.
\]

defs.def:empirical-projector:
Order the eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix \(A\) by decreasing absolute value, breaking equal-absolute-value ties by decreasing signed value.  Within every remaining repeated eigenspace, choose the orthonormal basis obtained by applying Gram--Schmidt to the nonzero vectors in the ordered list of projections of \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) onto that eigenspace.  Let \(\widehat\Psi_r(A)\) contain the first \(r\) resulting orthonormal eigenvectors and define
\[

defs.def:empirical-projector:
Order the eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix \(A\) by decreasing absolute value, breaking equal-absolute-value ties by decreasing signed value. \[

\]

defs.def:empirical-projector:
Order the eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix \(A\) by decreasing absolute value, breaking equal-absolute-value ties by decreasing signed value.  Within every remaining repeated eigenspace, choose the orthonormal basis obtained by applying Gram--Schmidt to the nonzero vectors in the ordered list of projections of \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) onto that eigenspace.  Let \(\widehat\Psi_r(A)\) contain the first \(r\) resulting orthonormal eigenvectors and define
\[
 \widehat\Pi_r(A)=\widehat\Psi_r(A)\widehat\Psi_r(A)^\top.
\]
This deterministic tie rule makes \(A\mapsto\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) a fixed Borel-measurable sample map.

defs.def:empirical-projector:

Let \(\widehat\Psi_r(A)\) contain the first \(r\) resulting orthonormal eigenvectors and define
\[
 \widehat\Pi_r(A)=\widehat\Psi_r(A)\widehat\Psi_r(A)^\top.
\]
This deterministic tie rule makes \(A\mapsto\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) a fixed Borel-measurable sample map.

defs.def:empirical-projector:
Put \(m_{r,n}=\min\{r,n\}\).  Order the \(n\) eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix \(A\) by decreasing absolute value, breaking equal-absolute-value ties by decreasing signed value.  Within every remaining repeated eigenspace, choose the orthonormal basis obtained by applying Gram--Schmidt to the nonzero vectors in the ordered list of projections of \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) onto that eigenspace.  Let \(\widehat\Psi_r(A)\in\mathbb R^{n\times m_{r,n}}\) contain the first \(m_{r,n}\) resulting orthonormal eigenvectors and define
\[
 \widehat\Pi_r(A)=\widehat\Psi_r(A)\widehat\Psi_r(A)^\top.
\]
Thus \(\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) is the orthogonal spectral projector onto the leading \(\min\{r,n\}\)-dimensional eigenspace selected by this convention.  The deterministic tie rule makes \(A\mapsto\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) a fixed Borel-measurable sample map for every \(r,n\in\mathbb N\), without requiring \(r\leq n\).

defs.def:empirical-projector:
Put \(m_{r,n}=\min\{r,n\}\).  Order the \(n\) eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix \(A\) by decreasing absolute value, breaking equal-absolute-value ties by decreasing signed value.  Within every remaining repeated eigenspace, choose the orthonormal basis obtained by applying Gram--Schmidt to the nonzero vectors in the ordered list of projections of \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) onto that eigenspace.  Let \(\widehat\Psi_r(A)\in\mathbb R^{n\times m_{r,n}}\) contain the first \(m_{r,n}\) resulting orthonormal eigenvectors and define
\[
 \widehat\Pi_r(A)=\widehat\Psi_r(A)\widehat\Psi_r(A)^\top.
\]
Thus \(\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) is the orthogonal spectral projector onto the leading \(\min\{r,n\}\)-dimensional eigenspace selected by this convention.  The deterministic tie rule makes \(A\mapsto\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) a fixed Borel-measurable sample map for every \(r,n\in\mathbb N\), without requiring \(r\leq n\).

defs.def:operational-bandwidth:

\[

\[

defs.def:radii:

For \(F_h(Z)=\widehat\theta_h\), define
\[
 c_{j,h}=\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\beta_{ij,h}.
\]
Conditional on \(A\) and the preassignment response functions, every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\) satisfies
\[
 |F_h(z)-F_h(z^{(j)})|\leq c_{j,h},
 \qquad
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal V_n}c_{j,h}^2
 =4\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}=4\overline s_h(A)^2,
\]
where \(z^{(j)}\) differs from \(z\) only in coordinate \(j\), and
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z(\widehat\theta_h-\theta_n\mid A,(f_i)_i)\right|
 \leq\overline b_h(A),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(\widehat\theta_h\mid A,(f_i)_i)
 \leq\overline s_h(A)^2.
\]
Consequently the conditional bounded-differences inequality gives
\[
 \Pr_Z\!\left\{
 |\widehat\theta_h-\mathbb E_Z(\widehat\theta_h\mid A,(f_i)_i)|
 >\overline s_h(A)\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)}
 \mathrel{\Big|}A,(f_i)_i\right\}\leq\alpha,
\]
and hence
\[
 \Pr_Z\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_h\mid A,(f_i)_i\}\geq1-\alpha.
\]
Because \(\widehat h(A)\) is fixed under this conditioning, every displayed certificate and the conditional coverage conclusion remain valid with \(h=\widehat h(A)\). \[
 G_A(C_A)=\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}(C_A)_{ij}^2,
\]

\[
 \widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
 \leq \frac{2B}{n}\|C_A\|_*
      +B\sqrt{\frac{G_A(C_A)}{n}}.
\]
The exact first two Hoeffding projections create no bandwidth-dependent term.  No rates \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}=O_P(d/n)\), \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}=O_P(d/n)\), or \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\lesssim\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\) are asserted.

 +\frac{B}{n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}
 +\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
\]

\[
 \overline s_h(A)^2=\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}.

snapshot.stmt:
For \(1\leq k\leq r\), let \(I_k=[(k-1)/r,k/r)\), with \(1\) included in \(I_r\), put \(\psi_k(u)=\sqrt r\,\mathbf 1\{u\in I_k\}\), and set
\[
 c_0=\max\{r/\kappa,r\underline\lambda\},
 \qquad
 W_0(u,v)=c_0\mathbf 1\{u\text{ and }v\text{ belong to the same }I_k\}.
\]
Suppose, in addition to the conditions defining \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), that
\[
 c_0\leq\kappa,
 \qquad
 b_\psi\geq (r-1)/\sqrt r.
\]
Let \(s_0=B/4\), let \(\xi_i\) be i.i.d. with density \(p_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1}\cos^2(\pi t/(2s_0))\mathbf 1\{|t|\leq s_0\}\), and use response pairs \(f_i^\pm(a,x)=\xi_i\pm g(x)\), with the three functions \(g\) constructed in the proof.  Then \(W_0\) and these random-intercept response laws generate an explicit block submodel of \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\).  Along sequences with \(B,L,r,\kappa,\underline\lambda,b_\psi,\alpha,C_{\log}\) fixed and \(C_{\log}\log n\leq d=o(n)\), there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(n\) and \(d\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
Within this same block submodel, respectively, a degree-lattice bump, an interior \(C^3\) bump, and a linear response pair furnish the lattice term, the interior nonlinear term for both absolute risk and honest expected length, and the graph floor.  The two displayed compatibility inequalities are only sufficient conditions for this explicit block witness and do not characterize nonemptiness; \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) separately proves the same supported lower benchmark over every eventually nonempty repaired class.

defs.def:lattice-radius: For \(N\ge1\), set \(\delta_N=N^{-1}\) when \(N\) is even and \(\delta_N=(2N)^{-1}\) when \(N\) is odd; for each \(i\) with \(N_i>0\), set \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\).
defs.def:minimax-criteria: At every index for which \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), let \(D=(A,Z,(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i\in\mathcal V_n})\). Define \(R^*_{n,d,L}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\theta-\theta_n|\), where the infimum ranges over all real-valued measurable estimators \(\widetilde\theta=\widetilde\theta(D)\). Define \(\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)=\inf_{\mathcal C}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[u(D)-\ell(D)]\), where the infimum ranges over data-measurable closed intervals \(\mathcal C(D)=[\ell(D),u(D)]\) with finite measurable endpoints \(\ell(D)\leq u(D)\) and satisfying \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C(D)\}\geq1-\alpha\). For every such interval, \(\operatorname{length}\{\mathcal C(D)\}=u(D)-\ell(D)\).

snapshot.stmt:
For \(L>0\), at every sufficiently large triangular-array index the supported-unit component satisfies \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp Ld^{-2}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\leq d^{-1}\), \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), and \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\geq d^{-1/2}\).  At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), the operational graph-adaptive selector satisfies
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \leq2\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)}\,\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\]
Along every sequence covered by the unrestricted supported converse, there is a constant \(c>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
Every graph-only conditional-bias certificate over the maintained class retains at least \(Bn^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}\) on a realized graph.  The explicit compatible block-submodel lower bound transfers upward only to the maintained class, and the unrestricted converse proves the maintained-class lower benchmark directly; neither result transfers automatically to the nonnested LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem~6 regime or its distinct finite indirect-effect target.  No bound \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\lesssim\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\) is proved, so the three analytic phases remain tuning geometry and a minimax lower benchmark rather than a sharp or achieved frontier.

defs.def:empirical-projector:
Put \(m_{r,n}=\min\{r,n\}\).  Order the \(n\) eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix \(A\) by decreasing absolute value, breaking equal-absolute-value ties by decreasing signed value.  Within every remaining repeated eigenspace, choose the orthonormal basis obtained by applying Gram--Schmidt to the nonzero vectors in the ordered list of projections of \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) onto that eigenspace.  Let \(\widehat\Psi_r(A)\in\mathbb R^{n\times m_{r,n}}\) contain the first \(m_{r,n}\) resulting orthonormal eigenvectors and define
\[
 \widehat\Pi_r(A)=\widehat\Psi_r(A)\widehat\Psi_r(A)^\top.
\]
Thus \(\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) is the orthogonal spectral projector onto the leading \(\min\{r,n\}\)-dimensional eigenspace selected by this convention.  The deterministic tie rule makes \(A\mapsto\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) a fixed Borel-measurable sample map for every \(r,n\in\mathbb N\), without requiring \(r\leq n\).
defs.def:estimator:
With the explicit score from \({\rm def:pc-handle}\),
\[
 \widehat\theta_h
 =\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}
 \left[q_{i,h}-4\left\{\widehat\Pi_r(A)A
       (Z-\tfrac12\mathbf1_n)\right\}_i\right]Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]
defs.def:exact-optimal-bandwidth:

\[
 h^\dagger=\min\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P[\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)].
\]
This is the oracle full-class radius-minimizing bandwidth.  Its evaluation requires the full-class supremum and is not an operational data-driven tuning rule.

defs.def:operational-bandwidth:
At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\), put \(\ell=d^{-1}\), \(u=\min\{d^{-1/2},1/2\}\), and, for each realized graph \(A\), define the finite nonempty candidate set
\[
 \mathcal K(A)=\{\ell,u\}\cup
 \left\{\left|\frac m{N_i}-\frac12\right|:
 i\in\mathcal V_n,\ N_i>0,\ 0\leq m\leq N_i,\
 \ell\leq\left|\frac m{N_i}-\frac12\right|\leq u\right\}.
\]
The graph-adaptive operational bandwidth is
\[
 \widehat h(A)=\min\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\mathcal K(A)}
 \{\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)\}.
\]
All ties are therefore resolved deterministically toward the smallest candidate.  The construction uses only the observed graph, the known constants, and the finite-lattice certificates; it does not use \(Z\) or the observed outcomes.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(I_0(A)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}\).  Under the repaired class, any graph-only radius \(b(A)\) that is required to satisfy
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z(\widetilde\theta-\theta_n\mid A,(f_i)_i)\right|\leq b(A)
\]
for every response configuration in the conditional support must obey
\[
 b(A)\geq \frac{B}{n}I_0(A)
\]
on every realized graph.  Whenever \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) is nonempty, the independent-Rademacher response submodel \(f_i(a,x)=\varepsilon_iBx\) is admissible, and even a genie revealing every nonisolate sign leaves, conditionally on \(A\), Bayes absolute-error risk between
\[
 \frac{B}{\sqrt3\,n}\sqrt{I_0(A)}
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad
 \frac{B}{n}\sqrt{I_0(A)}.
\]
Thus the corresponding unconditional missing-sign fluctuation is of order \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E\sqrt{I_0(A)}\), which is no larger than the expected conditional radius \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E I_0(A)\).  This distinction neither constructs an unconditionally honest interval nor proves that every such interval must pay the graph-only conditional radius.

snapshot.stmt:
Conditional on \(A\) and \((f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the derivative target and the Li--Wager finite indirect effect satisfy
\[
 \left|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n\right|
 \le \frac{L}{8n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac{1}{N_i}
 +\frac{B}{n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf 1\{N_i=0\}.
\]
Moreover, along any maintained triangular-array sequence with fixed \(B\) and \(\kappa\) such that \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\log(\rho_n)/\log(n)>-1/2\), one has \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n=o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n})\). On the further intersection of such a sequence with every source hypothesis enumerated in \({\rm lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\), specialize the treatment probability to one half and, writing \(\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) for the nonnegative variance factor in the full standardizer \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) of Li--Wager's equation~(43) at the \(n\)-th law, additionally suppose that \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}>0\). Then the equation~(43) Gaussian limit centered at \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) transfers by an additive Slutsky argument to the same statistic centered at \(\theta_n\). This is an asymptotic comparator only on that intersection, not a theorem for every sequence in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), and it is not a finite-sample equality of the two targets.

defs.def:li-wager-target: At Bernoulli probability one half, \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}=4n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbb E_Z[Y_i(Z)(M_i-N_i/2)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}]\), equivalently the finite indirect effect in equation (1) of LiWager2022RandomGraph.
